bluf: Cardinal Digital Marketing is a US healthcare only performance agency selling paid media, media mix modeling and business intelligence to multi location provider groups, DSOs and health systems. It does what it says: the record shows 134 Google ads of its own, 87 in the last 30 days, 24+ LinkedIn ads and a Scaling Up Summit. Where it is going the record does not say: no dated moves, no pricing, zero named clients. The one thing a rival should know: its sold mix sits on paid search and paid social, the lines the Horus read says the platforms are absorbing, and it shows no AI assistant ad test.
doing:
Cardinal positions itself as a healthcare only performance marketing agency for multi location provider groups, DSOs and health systems, pairing paid media with media mix modeling and business intelligence. In plain words: a vertical paid media shop that sells the measurement layer on top of the media so enterprise health groups can plan budgets across channels. Its headline claim is 14 years scaling the nation's largest healthcare groups, with a 77% conversion lift for the largest PT group as the proof point; the claim is the agency's own and no named case study sits in the record.

The sold mix leads with data and measurement (scored 3: the proprietary RevRx channel mix and budget planning tool and media mix modeling on the homepage, plus a business intelligence service page) and paid search (scored 3: performance marketing heads the title and H1, and the PPC case lifts CVR 77% for the largest PT group). Paid social scores 2 on a dedicated Meta advertising page for full funnel Facebook and Instagram campaigns, with TikTok Ads also listed. The service list adds display and video ads, performance creative, patient acquisition strategy, website design and MSO digital strategy. RevRx is the only proprietary product; the record lists no partners.

AI posture is light: it lists SEO & AISO (AI optimised search) as a capability and shows no AI product or automation offer; AI search scores 1 and AI automation 0. The moves list is empty, and no news, case studies or jobs were captured, so the record holds no dated move to sequence. Pricing signals: none; no public pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a healthcare performance agency of its kind: any CRM, email or owned audience line (email and CRM scores 0), any content or digital PR line (also 0), and local work scored only 1 with no LSA evidence, for a business built on multi location providers.
clients:
The record types the client as enterprise: multi location provider groups, DSOs and health systems, and the verticals list runs healthcare, multi location provider groups, dental (DSOs), behavioral health, health systems, primary care, veterinary, dermatology and physical therapy. The home market is the US; no office city is listed.

The needs read is empty: 0 clients, 0 observed, 0 named only, no mix and no shared clients, because the crawl captured no case study pages or client names. The only client the record describes is unnamed: the largest PT group, credited with a 77% conversion lift in a PPC case on the homepage, which reads as a paid performance need observed as a claim rather than a named engagement. The rest of the book is not names only, it is absent, which is itself a finding for an agency claiming 14 years with the nation's largest healthcare groups.

The nearest thing to a client list is the LinkedIn ad copy for its Scaling Up Summit, which names marketing leaders from Sutter Health, Keck Medicine of USC, Action Behavior Centers, Tend Dental and AllerVie Health as speakers; the record does not say whether any is a client, so they are relationships, not engagements. No shared clients can be computed against other tracked agencies.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places the mix best for KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better), driven by its data and measurement line, and KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), and most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer). It is likely, with moderate confidence, that enterprise health groups buying paid media will ask for the measurement and mix modeling that RevRx already sells more than for media execution, the line the platforms are taking in house.
house:
Say and do: 3 of 3 tested lines are practised on its own house. Paid search is corroborated: it runs its own Google ads, 134 in the Transparency Center and 87 in the last 30 days, split 15 text, 65 image and 54 video, under the advertiser name Cardinal Web Solutions, last shown 2026-09-27. Paid social is corroborated by meta_pixel and linkedin_insight on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated with 24+ company page ads and 0 thought leader ads; one sample reads: Before you lock your 2027 budget, hear what healthcare marketing leaders are prioritizing, cutting, and testing. The Radar flagged no gaps.

The stack is WordPress with GTM, GA4, HubSpot and Dealfront Leadfeeder as an ABM tool; no testing tools were detected. Content velocity is the weak point: the sitemap read returned 0 URLs, 0 updated in 90 days and 0 in 365, and there is no llms.txt, no AI crawler blocks and 0 AI URLs.
market:
The Horus read scores Cardinal at a tailwind index of 8.6, band Neutral, say and do integrity 100. Best placed for KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better, driven by data and measurement) and KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation, with AI search and paid search positive). Most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, paid search and paid social at -2 each). Best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 58/100. Moves: making P4 (supply the inputs automation runs on), partial on P1, unknown on P5, absent on P2, P3, P6, P7 and P8.

The Monsoon read: index 52.6, band Breeze; migration 55.1 against displacement 50.1, an enterprise ICP term of -5 holding displacement down. The verdict puts 55 of the index on the sold mix, paid search (14) and data and measurement (11) the most movable hours, sends the work 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America, with automation overlapping 35% of the movable hours, all inferred: no hub office or onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the execution layer. Cardinal sells paid search and paid social to enterprise health groups, and the Horus read makes KJ4 its largest exposure, driven by paid search: the hours it bills are the hours the platforms' automation removes. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival selling measurement and mix modeling without the media markup, or offering the media at outcome pricing, can pull budget from the same provider groups. Falsifier: a Cardinal case study or pricing page showing media fees tied to patient acquisition outcomes rather than spend.

Second, no sign of testing ads inside AI assistants on a paid search book: the first healthcare agency to show assistant ad results with holdouts sets the price. Third, no public pricing model, so an outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot hold in public. Fourth, the empty client book: with 0 named clients, a rival with named DSO and health system cases has more proof, which very likely (high confidence) matters in enterprise procurement. The Monsoon read is Breeze at 52.6, so a price undercut alone is unlikely to move this book; the measurement and AI visibility gap is the better lead.
watch: I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the paid search line, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and raises the cost of the absent P8 test.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.

I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and its timing, and pricing below $20 CPM, would signal supply outrunning demand and make assistant ads a cheap place for a healthcare rival to test first.

No dated move sits in the record; the follow up is the Scaling Up Summit its LinkedIn ads count down three weeks to, and whether the speakers it names from Sutter Health and Keck Medicine of USC surface as clients.

The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile, and the empty sitemap read is the first thing a recompile should settle.
